block.label: WARM-UP
block.html: Quick answers, then one follow-up question each. Just warming up!

cats.name: You
qs: How was your week, honestly? One high, one low.
Did you have pets growing up? Tell me about the most memorable one.
Dog person, cat person, or neither? Defend your answer.

If an animal could represent your personality, which one would it be?

models.title: In the news · the 1,200-year-old mummified dog (Peru)

block.label: IN THE NEWS · A 1,200-YEAR-OLD MUMMIFIED DOG
block.html:
On Peru's northern desert coast, about 300 km north of Lima, lies Castillo de Huarmey, a burial ground of the Wari, a civilization that flourished centuries before the Incas (around 600–1050 CE). The bone-dry desert has preserved what usually rots away: skin, hair, textiles.

Among the finds, archaeologists have identified the remains of at least 19 dogs, and three of them appear to be Peruvian hairless dogs, a breed that still exists today. One skull was naturally mummified, with patches of bare skin, its ears still attached, and traces of red cinnabar, a pigment used in funeral rituals.

At first, the team suspected the bones belonged to modern dogs, dumped there by 20th-century looters. The giveaway was in the teeth: some of them never formed, a quirk of the same gene that makes the breed hairless.

Chemical analysis suggests the hairless puppies were fed like human children, on a maize-rich diet, which hints that people cared for them closely and may have controlled their breeding. One puppy was buried beside an elite craftsman nicknamed the Master Basketmaker. Hairless dogs also appear in Wari art more than any other domestic animal.

Not every dog was so lucky, though. Others ended up in rubbish heaps, on the fringes of daily life. Today, the breed, perro sin pelo del Perú, is officially part of Peru's national heritage.

Teacher: search images for perro sin pelo del Perú and show one on the shared screen before reading.

block.label: FIRST REACTIONS
block.html: React to the story. No right answers: go deep, disagree, tell stories.

cats.name: The story
qs: What was your first reaction to the photo? Cute, ugly, or fascinating?
Why do you think elite people were buried with dogs? What does that say about them?
The puppies ate like human children. Were the Wari the first "pet parents"?
The scientists first thought it was a modern dog dumped by looters. What does that tell you about how science works?
Peru made a dog breed part of its national heritage. What would Brazil choose as a "living national treasure"?

models.title: Discussion · from the dog to everything else

block.label: DISCUSSION · FROM ONE DOG TO EVERYTHING
block.html: Pick the tab that sounds most interesting. It's fine to jump between topics: the dog is just the door.

cats.name: Pets as family
qs: Some couples now call their dogs "kids". Is that sweet, sad, or just honest?
IBGE once found more dogs than children in Brazilian homes. Why do you think that is?
Pet funerals, pet insurance, pet strollers: where is the line between love and excess?
Courts in Brazil have given divorced couples visiting rights to their dog. Fair, or ridiculous?
Would you leave money in your will to a pet? Who should take care of it?

cats.name: Death & legacy
qs: The Wari were buried with what mattered to them. What would you want to be buried with?
Burial, cremation, or something else? Have you ever thought about it?
In 1,200 years, archaeologists dig up your neighborhood. What will they get completely wrong about us?
What do you want to be remembered for? Not your job: something else.
Do you keep objects from people who have died? Which one means the most to you?

cats.name: History & the past
qs: Most Brazilians know very little about the peoples who lived here before 1500. Why?
Which ancient civilization fascinates you the most, and why?
Should museums return objects to the countries they were taken from?
Brazil lost most of the Museu Nacional collection in the 2018 fire. Whose fault is that kind of loss?
If you could spend one day in any period of history, where and when would you go?

cats.name: Ethics
qs: Breeding dogs for a 'look' (flat faces, no hair) can cause health problems. Should it be banned?
Adopt or buy? Is it wrong to buy a pedigree dog when shelters are full?
We love dogs and eat pigs, which are just as intelligent. Is that hypocritical?
Is digging up an ancient grave science, or a kind of grave robbing?
Should animals have legal rights? Which ones?

models.title: Speculating about the past · must / might / can't have

block.label: LANGUAGE · SPECULATING ABOUT THE PAST
block.html:
Archaeologists never know for sure. They speculate. So do we:

must have + form 3 → I'm almost sure it's true.
This dog must have been very important to its owner.

might / may / could have + form 3 → maybe.
It might have been a gift to the dead.

can't / couldn't have + form 3 → I'm almost sure it's not true.
It can't have been a modern dog: look at its teeth.

⚠️ Brazilian trap: deve ter sido = must have been, not had to be.
✗ He had to be rich to have a dog like that. (= he was obliged to be rich)
✓ He must have been rich to have a dog like that.

🗣️ In fast speech: must've, might've, could've /ˈmʌstəv/ · and never ✗ must of.

models.title: Future archaeologists · speculate about our objects

block.label: GAME · ARCHAEOLOGISTS IN THE YEAR 3226
block.html:
It's the year 3226. You are an archaeologist, and you have just dug up an object from the 21st century, with no context. Draw a card and speculate about what it was for, using the structure on the card. The sillier and more convincing, the better!
A flip-flop? People must have worn it in religious ceremonies. It can't have been for walking: it has no back!
prompts: must have + one more guess with might have

models.title: Devil's advocate · argue the side you don't believe

block.label: DEVIL'S ADVOCATE
block.html:
Draw a statement and a side. Argue it for one minute, even if you disagree. Then say what you really think.
Useful: Let me play devil's advocate here… · The way I see it… · I take your point, but… · That's a slippery slope.
lines: Pets should be allowed in restaurants, offices and planes.
Spending R$10,000 on a pet's surgery is perfectly reasonable.
Museums should return every object taken from another country.
Breeding animals for their looks should be illegal.
It's hypocritical to love dogs and eat pigs.
Digging up ancient graves is just grave robbing with a diploma.
Calling your dog your "son" is perfectly normal.
People who can afford a pedigree dog should adopt one instead.

block.label: DOG IDIOMS · TELL ME ABOUT…
block.html: Answer with a real story, and use the idiom in your answer.

cats.name: Idioms
qs: Tell me about a time you were in the doghouse. What did you do to get out?
Is there a topic in your family where it is better to let sleeping dogs lie?
Is your industry a dog-eat-dog world? Which industry is the worst?
Tell me about a time you were barking up the wrong tree.
What do you think has gone to the dogs in the last 10 years? What has got better?
When was the last time you worked like a dog? Was it worth it?

models.title: Role-play · who keeps the dog? (divorce mediation)

block.label: ROLE-PLAY · WHO KEEPS THE DOG?
block.html:
The situation: Paula and Rafael are getting divorced. They agree on everything except Mel, their 6-year-old dog. Both want her.

Alyson is Rafael: he found Mel on the street and paid for her surgery, but he travels for work two weeks a month.
The teacher is Paula: she walks Mel every day and works from home, but she is moving to a small apartment without a yard.

Round 1: argue your case to the mediator (3 minutes).
Round 2: switch roles!
Round 3: you are the judge. Decide, and justify your decision. Shared custody? Visits? Who pays the vet?

Useful: With all due respect… · Let's be realistic here… · I'm willing to compromise on… · That's a deal-breaker for me.
